items.markdown: g), and an even stronger increase in phosphorylated cofilin (Supplementary Fig. 10f, h). Interestingly, this effect was abolished upon co-treatment with JSH-23. Taken together, these results suggest that inflammatory conditions promote F-actin stabilization through cofilin inactivation, supporting the formation of TNT-like structures. To understand whether molecular changes are also associated with global re-organization of the actin cytoskeletal network, we

measured the coherency of actin filaments<sup>69</sup> in experimental conditions where α-Syn-induced intercellular connections were shown to depend on NF-κB (Fig. 5d). A higher coherency of actin filaments would be expected upon directional re-organization of the network (Supplementary Fig. 6i), a phenotype expected during the formation of TNTs.
